knowledgeAnswers.rationale: A balance sheet is dated and shows assets, liabilities and equity at that date. Cash received over a year belongs to a cash record, not a balance sheet.
A receivable exists only after work is done and invoiced. Quotes, accepted or not, are not assets.
Equity equals total assets less total liabilities: 50,000 less 30,000 gives 20,000.

practicalCriteria: Learner produces a balance sheet at one stated date in which total assets equal total liabilities plus equity
No uninvoiced quote or unaccepted job appears as a receivable
Each long-term asset is shown after depreciation, with the method stated
Learner finds the seeded imbalance in an assessor-supplied statement and traces it to a specific line
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Completed working document for the lesson, saved with its formulas or calculation notes
Knowledge check result (a quiz result is not a practical competence result)
stopWorkCriteria: Do not present a balance sheet that does not balance
Stop and escalate any receivable that is not backed by an issued invoice
Escalate depreciation and drawings treatment to a registered tax agent
